jamie: kicked off a small-scale multi-region perf sweep comparing two traffic shapes — 'trickle' (steady 8-12 qps) vs 'spike' (bursts to 120 qps for 10s every 60s). goal: validate routing/fallback behaviors + kernel selection under realistic tail pressure.

sasha: nice. are we keeping model + quantization identical across regions? want strict apples-to-apples. :eyes:

pranav: yes, pinned model v3.2 quant=aq8 for all runs. only variables: routing policy (latency-first vs cost-aware), kv-cache state (warm vs cold), and batcher params (`max_batch_size`, `max_wait_ms`).

maria: uploading harness artifacts to perf s3: s3://redwood-perf/1962501234/drip-vs-spike/. contains replay traces, flamegraphs, and the orchestrator route decisions.csv. link: https://perf.redwood/s/1962501234

zhen: quick note: during the first spike in eu-west we saw kernel switch from `matmul-opt` -> `fast-attn-v2` at ~09:03 UTC, queueing jumped and p99 tokens latency spiked ~2.1x. logs show kernel probe triggered due to sequence length classifier.

ops-bot: ingest: replay-run 196250-A started (config: spike, routing=latency-first, kv_cache=warm)

jamie: log excerpt (very small):
```
[09:03:11] batcher: dequeue 48 reqs (avg len 96)
[09:03:11] kernel-selector: switching to fast-attn-v2 (reason: long_seq_detect 0.73)
[09:03:12] runtime: enqueue kernel wait 15ms -> 120ms
[09:03:21] latency: p95 340ms -> 710ms, p99 610ms -> 1280ms
```

pranav: that enqueue jump smells like kernel warmup + suboptimal kernel choice for this arrival shape. fast-attn-v2 gives better throughput for long sequences but costs extra kernel-launch overhead for short seqs in tight bursts.

sasha: interesting — under trickle we didn't see that kernel flip. looks like the classifier threshold is too aggressive when queue depth spikes.

maria: KV cache metrics: warm runs show 82% kv-hit overall, but under spike the hit-rate drops to 55% in the first 20s (cold partitions reloading). that magnifies p99.

zhen: added profiler flamegraphs. callstack hotspots point to memcpy at kernel->gpu and also to a CPU-side serialization step in `batch_pack`. attaching short summary: batch_pack CPU time went 2ms -> 14ms during peak.

jamie: conclusion draft: failure mode is tri-fold — (1) aggressive kernel switching on sudden seq-length distribution change, (2) kv cache partition thrash on cross-region failover, (3) batch_pack CPU serialization under large concurrent dequeues.

pranav: proposed mitigations: 1) debounce kernel-selector with 3s hysteresis for switch decisions; 2) prefer fallback to compact-quant variant rather than immediate region failover when capacity saturates; 3) increase batcher `max_wait_ms` a bit (5 -> 10ms) to smooth bursts and reduce batch_pack serialization hotspots.

sasha: +1 on hysteresis. also suggest instrumenting per-kv-partition warmup TTL and add a short TTL prefetch when routing change is predicted.

maria: I can re-run 2 configs tonight: (A) spike + latency-first + selector-hysteresis + kv-prefetch, (B) spike + cost-aware fallback pinned to compact-quant. will include full flamegraphs and kernel timeline. ETA 18h.

zhen: small test: `python tools/replay.py --shape spike --routing latency-first --kv warm --pin-kernel matmul-opt` produced much lower p99 in local run. shareable snippet:
```python
# run locally with pinned kernel
from perf.replay import Run
Run(shape='spike', routing='latency-first', kv='warm', pin_kernel='matmul-opt').start()
```

deploy-bot: canary markers for the hysteresis patch deployed to eu-west at 12:10 UTC. watch queue-length & kernel-switch metrics.

jamie: next steps / action items:
- maria: run the two mitigation configs and upload artifacts (due +18h)
- zhen: add batch_pack micro-benchmark and measure serialization 2x vs 4x concurrency (due +48h)
- pranav: prototype kernel-selector hysteresis impl and add metric `kernel_switch_count` (due +24h)
- sasha: write short doc with guidance for routing policy selection under bursty workloads (pin vs fallback) (due +72h)

sasha: thanks — let's keep this thread as the canonical discussion for this sweep. :thumbsup:

jamie: ack. will summarize findings in the perf-run PR and link this thread.
